newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Focus-Bank of Ireland interim profits up slightly.
newsitem.headline: Focus-Bank of Ireland interim profits up slightly.

text.p: Bank of Ireland, one of Ireland's largest banking and financial services groups, said on Thursday that half-year pre-tax profit was 193.1 million punts ($319.8 million), marginally ahead of last year.
The bank said its retail division recorded very good growth with pre-tax profit rising by 6.4 percent to 104.4 million punts as deposits and lending volumes in Ireland and Britain rose.
But profits in its corporate and treasury division fell by 11 percent to 36.9 million as treasury income slipped from exceptionally high levels seen in the first half of 1995.

The bank's other activities, which include its asset management arm, its life assurance unit and Davy Stockbrokers, rose by 15 percent to 42.1 million while its U.S. operations contributed 13.5 million to group profits.
The results were within analysts' expectations which ranged from 190 to 194 million punts.
"The results were bang in line with expectations and those expectations were conditioned by the fact that this is very much a transition year," chief executive Pat Molloy said.
In April, Bank of Ireland merged its U.S. operation, First Holdings, with Royal Bank of Scotland's Citzens Financial Group in which it now has a 23.5 percent interest.
This involved a number of once-off restructuring costs and also has a significant after-tax effect as Bank of Ireland's U.S. earnings are now taxable.

It also announced it was acquiring Bristol & West, Britain's ninth largest building society, for 600 million pounds ($991.1 million) in April while a number of restructuring projects are under way in its retail division.
"It's a transition year in those respects but at the end of it all I think we are going to be very strongly positioned for continuing growth," Molloy told Reuters.
He said the group was paying for Bristol & West in cash which meant it would not have a lot of spending power left after the acquisition was completed in mid-1997.
"We will begin to build capital thereafter relatively quickly. That is going to be the dominant issue for us in the course of the next calendar year."
Bank of Ireland announced an interim dividend of 6.1 Irish pence per share, up from 5.0 pence in the first half of 1995. Its share price was unchanged at 511 pence by 1045 GMT.
